posts.author: Raghav_Pateriya
posts.text: I don’t think stock price makes sense. I have invested in it. I think market is thinking Cell manufacturing is not as challenging as before. Chinese assembly line kits have made it “commoditised”. Current ALMM-2 compliant capacity is 27 GW but with Waree, Adani, Premier, Reliance, Vikram etc announcing massive capex, 80 GW more is in pipeline for next 2 years. Annual demand in India is 40-50 GW per year. So massive capex + low implied utilisation = potential balance sheet disaster. For Websol, management’s long term target 4GW. posts.text: Key takeaways of meeting with management Their current utilization is 92% for cell and 81% for module They have achieved net debt free status this quarter They are upgrading 1 line to topcon, will give them incremental capacity of 150MW. It will also train their people for new topcon plant For new plant, location was changed as investment climate has improved in WB and proximity to old plant will increase efficiency. posts.author: Niki14
posts.text: I have to say that this stock has been devastating for investors. The management is least bothered about establishing proper communication with investors on a regular basis. They might be churning profits but are unable to bring investment from even domestic institutes. The stock will go down to 78 levels as of now.

posts.author: ankiur.jain83
posts.text: Websol’s results posted decent results but SM is filled with people worrying about Websol’s profit margin’s reducing this quarter. If market’s already did not factor this in, then why would a company growing revenue at 70%+ y-o-y basis be trading at PE of 13? It’s only margin’s falling, not the profit’s falling in absolute numbers. From last 2-3 quarters their cell line was already working at 90%+ capacity.
